_comment: Input for scripts/build_quicksetup.py. Every file in source_dir must have an entry in 'steps' (its instruction lines) or in 'excluded' (with the reason) -- a new source file fails `--check` until someone decides which.

pq.preamble:
==============================================================================
CONSOLIDATED POWER QUERY REFERENCE -- all queries, in the order to add them
==============================================================================

This file is a READ-ALONG REFERENCE, not something to paste as a whole.
Power BI's Advanced Editor holds exactly ONE query per paste. For each
section below: New Blank Query > Home > Advanced Editor > paste that
section's M code > OK > rename the query to the name shown > Close & Apply
when done with all of them. Having ONE file open (this one) instead of
{n_files} separate files is the time-saving here.

00_Parameters.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: pRootFolder (Manage Parameters, NOT a Blank Query)
# NOTE: Home > Transform data > Manage Parameters > New.
01_fnCombineFolder.pq: # NOTE: Blank Query > Advanced Editor > paste > rename.
10_Fact_PrimarySales.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Primary Sales
11_Fact_OfftakeSales.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Offtake Sales
13_Fact_Nielsen.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Nielsen Market Share
15_Fact_PrimaryShipTo.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Primary ShipTo
16_Fact_PrimaryArticle.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Primary Article
20_Dim_Masters.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Chain Master, Brand Master, Category Master, Article Master, Zone State Master, Store Master, Nielsen Competitor Master
# NOTE: SEVEN separate queries -- one per '---------- X Master ----------' block in the file below. Each block is its own complete `let...in` query; uncomment/copy ONE block at a time.
22_CustomerCodeZoneMaster.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Customer Code Zone Master
24_ChannelMap.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Channel Map Store, Channel Map Chain
# NOTE: TWO separate queries -- one per block in the file below.
34_PrimaryAllocationMap.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Primary Allocation Map
35_PrimaryAllocationOverride.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Primary Allocation Override
36_SalesTeamMapping.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Sales Team Mapping
37_GST_Rate_QC_Table.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: GST Rate QC Table
39_PL_Expense_Input.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: PL Expense Input
40_CustCode_Chain_Map.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: CustCode Chain Map
# NOTE: Add AFTER Fact Primary Article (query 16) -- depends on it.
41_DistContWeights.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Dist Cont Weights
42_PackSizeBuckets.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Pack Size Buckets
# NOTE: Reads Fact Offtake Sales and Fact Primary Article -- add after both.
43_SecondarySalesEfficiency.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Secondary Sales Efficiency
# NOTE: Reads Fact Offtake Sales and Fact Primary Article -- add after both.
44_Fact_SecondarySales.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Secondary Sales
45_Fact_ClaimMaster.pq: # RENAME QUERY TO: Fact Claim Master

excluded.46_Dim_PromoCalendar.pq: Not usable in Desktop yet: loads File.Contents("PowerBI/RawDataFolders/Promo_Calendar/promo_mechanics_Sep_2026.csv") -- a relative path fixed to one month, not pRootFolder + the folder -- and its relationship notes name tables this model does not have (Dim_Brand, Dim_Calendar, Dim_Chain). Needs its own fix before it can be a setup step.

dax.preamble:
==============================================================================
CONSOLIDATED DAX REFERENCE -- all measures/columns, in the order to add them
==============================================================================

This file is a READ-ALONG REFERENCE, not something to paste as a whole.
Power BI's New Measure formula bar holds exactly ONE measure at a time.
For each measure below: select the _Measures table > New Measure > paste
ONE 'Name = Expression' block (including any VAR/RETURN lines that belong
to it) > Enter. Having ONE file open (this one) instead of {n_files} separate
files, with the calculated-column exceptions called out up front, is the
time-saving here.

*** READ THIS FIRST -- 6 blocks below are CALCULATED COLUMNS, not measures:
    - 'Fact Primary Article'[TOT Method]              (in 12_TOT_Measures)
    - 'Fact Primary Article'[TOT Pass-on Value]       (in 12_TOT_Measures)
    - 'PL Expense Input'[Resolved Chain]              (in 13_CM2_Measures)
    - 'PL Expense Input'[Resolved Brand]              (in 13_CM2_Measures)
    - 'PL Expense Input'[Resolved Category]           (in 13_CM2_Measures)
    - 'PL Expense Input'[Bad Brand Or Category]       (in 13_CM2_Measures)
    They are already commented out (//) in those two files below, exactly
    so you don't accidentally paste them as measures. Add each one via
    its OWN table (select the table > New column), not via New Measure.
    Every other measure in 12/13 IS a normal measure for _Measures.

00_DateTable.dax: # TARGET: Date Table (calculated TABLE, not a measure)
# NOTE: Modeling > New table > paste the WHOLE file as one calculated table. Then mark as date table on [Date]. NOT part of the _Measures bulk-paste below.
12_TOT_Measures.dax: # TARGET: _Measures table -- EXCEPT the commented-out 'Fact Primary Article'[TOT Method] / [TOT Pass-on Value] blocks near the top, which are CALCULATED COLUMNS on Fact Primary Article (add via that table > New column), not measures.
13_CM2_Measures.dax: # TARGET: _Measures table -- EXCEPT the commented-out 'PL Expense Input'[Resolved Chain] / [Resolved Brand] / [Resolved Category] / [Bad Brand Or Category] blocks near the top, which are CALCULATED COLUMNS on PL Expense Input (add via that table > New column), not measures.
14_SecondarySales_Measures.dax: # TARGET: _Measures table (needs query 44 Fact Secondary Sales loaded first)
# NOTE: measure names in this file are written as [Name] = ...; enter each as Name = ... (no brackets) in the New Measure bar.

excluded.15_Promo_Measures.dax: Not usable in this model yet: it reads tables no query builds (Fact_Secondary_TOT_Hierarchy; Fact_ClaimMaster -- query 45 builds 'Fact Claim Master') and Dim_PromoCalendar from the excluded query 46. Needs its own fix before it can be a setup step.
